newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen sliding below 113 yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen sliding below 113 yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to drift down and break below 113 yen during Asian trading time on Friday, vulnerable as a result of overnight falls in U.S. stocks and exporter selling interest, dealers said.

U.S. blue-chip stocks plunged nearly 100 points in the last hour of trading in the biggest points loss since mid-July. Dow industrials lost 1.54 percent to about 6,304. Stocks were pressured after a bond market rally withered.
Dealers predicted featureless Asian trade with eyes on the start later on Friday of the Dublin summit of European Union heads of state and government.
They said a key point for the market would be whether agreement was reached on the terms of a pact to enforce fiscal discipline after the launch of a single currency.

Germany is pressing for a strict definition of the circumstances in which countries running a fiscal deficit of more than three percent should be exempt from finds, while other countries want more flexibility.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that he was ready to find a good solution to the dispute. "In any case we are prepared to look for a good solution. But it must be appropriate to the subject," he told reporters in Dublin.
Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker told reporters: "We need a deal between a rigid mechanism and not an overly rigid mechanism."
Most in the market expect the negotiations to end in a relatively weak or ineffective pact, which would lead to increased dollar strength and put the mark under pressure.

Japanese operators would be reluctant to take out fresh positions ahead of the summit, making for sluggish trade during Asian time, dealers said. They said that although the dollar was expected to break below 113 yen, falls were likely to be halted near 112.60 yen on investor bids.
Importers were also expected to be interested in bargain-hunting, a city bank dealer said.
On the topside, exporter offers were expected to emerge from 113.30 yen on up, limiting the topside. "Any rise will be an excuse to take profits," a dealer at a trust bank said.
The mark was expected to remain firm against the yen, with its downside solidly supported near 73.10 yen.
